tips: Aatrox wins early, but all of his damage comes from landing his Q. Fleet Footwork helps us tremendously here because we’re able to dodge his Q more efficiently. Prioritize getting Phage and boots to help with dodging his Q as well.

Akali's all in potential doesn't come into play until she gets her ultimate. When she hits level six, this matchup becomes incredibly difficult because she's granted two damaging gap closers. Watch closely to her resource bar. Her Q will slow you if you are hit by the tip of it. When it comes to Akali's shroud, Gnar's ultimate is a good tool to push her out of it.

Camille has two gap closers that put Gnar in a huge disadvantage. You have the option to dodge her E with your E, but her E is on a significantly lower cooldown. Dodging her E is extremely vital in this matchup. Her second Q press does true damage, so you want to weave in and out of trades to avoid being hit by this. Prioritize getting Phage and boots to help with dodging her E and W.

Cassiopeia struggles early.
She scales really well, so look to make plays in lane.
Poke her with your Q.
Watch her mana closely because her abilities use a lot of it early.
Once she grabs her Tear, expect her to start spamming abilities.
Her W grounds, so you can't use your E or Flash in it.
You can outplay her R by juking backwards as soon as you see the animation start.
It'll only hit you if you're looking at her.
Cho’Gath has no way of closing the gap to you and he has to be very close to you in order to use his R. As long as you are dodging his Q and staying at a distance, you will destroy in this matchup.

This matchup can be easy depending on the summoner spell that Darius takes. If he takes Teleport, you can easily kite him out. If he takes Ghost, you absolutely need to be careful with your E and Flash. Generally, Darius starts trades with his Q and E. Watch for his Q cooldown and go in for trades if he misses you with the outside of it. If his Ghost is down, kiting Darius is extremely easy. Wait until you're level 7 to start trading. This is when Gnar's attack range outranges Darius' E.

Dodging Dr. Mundo’s Q is vital in this matchup. If you are avoiding his Q and are poking when you’re able, you should win this matchup with no issues. Because Dr. Mundo benefits from health items, Mini Gnar's W will shred through him.

Fiora can use her W to prevent your third W stack and your all in. Watch for this cooldown and abuse her when it’s down. Keep an eye on the position of her vitals, as this will be your main source of counterplay. A good tip for this matchup would be to hug the terrain that’s on the same side of her vitals when fighting her so she can’t proc it. Consider rushing Ninja Tabi.

Gnar wins early game over Gangplank. Once Gangplank finishes his Triforce, power starts to shift into Gangplank’s favor. The key to this lane is to dodge his exploding barrels. Avoid all inning as Mega Gnar when Gangplank has his W up because it removes CC. His W is on a long cooldown, so abuse him when he uses it.
Garen’s passive can easily be stopped with Gnar’s Q and AA. Focus on kiting Garen when he attempts to Q in for trades.

Gragas uses a lot of mana early. Abuse this. Gnar also has a lot of options to dodge all of his abilities. Always respect Gragas' R as it's an easy way for him to all-in you. You can Flash to the opposite side of his R as he throws it to be thrown into the opposite direction. Gnar's E can do this too, but it's harder to time.

Hecarim has an insane amount of sustain built into his W. He also has a gap closer on his E and R. You can Flash as soon as his E connects to be thrown into the direction you flashed instead of the direction his E would send you. Hecarim struggles before level 6.

Heimerdinger relies heavily on landing his E on you. When he lands his E, he gets full beam charge on his turrets. Make it your priority to dodge this. Another thing to keep in mind is that his ulted turret can't be displaced with your ult. You're going to get pushed in early, so look for ganks from your jungler. Look for all-in opportunities after you hit level six.

All of Illaoi’s all in potential revolves from her E. Dodging this is extremely vital. If you’re hit, walk back and avoid being hit by her tentacles. Her R will summon an extra tentacle if you get hit by her E. Illaoi’s E has a long animation, so dodging it is easy.

Irelia has so many options to close the gap against you. The key here is to keep an eye on your minions that are low on health. Irelia’s Q will reset if she kills a minion with it. You absolutely have to dodge her E because it applies her mark on you. Overall, you want Irelia to push in this matchup as much as possible. Keep your minion wave close to your tower and ask for ganks.

Jarvan IV is going to be looking to land his E → Q combo on you in lane. Dodging this is key because it's all of his damage. It's fairly easy to do so with Fleet Footwork and your passive. A good Jarvan IV will be able to E → Q → Flash, so keep that in mind. If his ult is down, he has no all-in potential. Abuse him when he has cooldowns.

Jax’s only way to trade with you early is his E, so abuse him when it's on cooldown. A good Jax will E → Q to catch your E, so try to time getting away as soon as you see his E animation. Once Jax finishes his Triforce, he becomes a powerhouse.

Jayce has a lot of damage he can deal at a distance. Avoiding his Q is extremely important. If you’re poked down enough, Jayce will switch to Hammer Stance and all in you. Sadly, it’s nearly impossible to all in Jayce when his E is up. He will knock you back as soon as you E in.

Karma can be a very annoying matchup because of the amount of shields and mobility she can pump out in a short amount of time. Her damage is weak early and she also has issues with mana. Look to all-in her after you hit level 6.

Kayle takes a good while to scale. Assuming both of you are even at level 11, Kayle wins. The gap is huge by level 16, so try your best to end the game before then. With that being said, look to gain leads on her before her power spikes. Poke her down with your Q. Look for all-ins at level six.

Kennen’s Q is his main resource for poke. Keep an eye on how many stacks of his passive he has on you. Once he gets three, you’ll be stunned. His E is a long cooldown and his only way to escape, so abuse him when it’s down. Kennen’s kill potential comes from his R. Sadly, his R animation is instant, so try and play outside of its range and keep note on his Flash cooldown. Mostly, you will see AP Kennen, so consider getting MR, but on the off chance you see AD Kennen, build accordingly.

Kled’s early game is phenomenal if he lands his Q and has his W up, so avoiding this is key. Most Kled players will attempt an all in at level three. Kled is a melee champion, so you can easily poke him down off of Skaarl. Be very careful of Kled remounting. His Q off of Skaarl will give him a big chunk of Courage if he hits you with it. He also gets bonus Courage when he autos champions, turrets, and monsters. Kled is also extremely good at diving because of his passive. If he chooses to go for a dive, Kled will lose turret aggro if he falls off Skaarl because he becomes untargetable for a short time.

Lissandra has a gap closer and plenty of disengage in her kit to allow her to be very safe in lane. You can catch her as she uses her E to get away with Mega Gnar's W and R. Look to all-in when her E is on cooldown.

Lucian's lane pressure makes it almost impossible to win trades as Mini Gnar early. Poke with your Q and play safe until level 6. Watch his E cooldown and look to all-in with Mega Gnar when it's on cooldown.

This matchup is difficult due to Malphite’s passive and E. His passive gives him an insane amount of health and armor. His E also lowers your attack speed, making it very difficult to proc your W. Luckily, Malphite is a melee champion, so we have a little freeway here.
Maokai is a melee champion, so poke him as much as possible. Keep an eye on his mana because his abilities will eat it. The only way he can close the gap is his W, but it’s on a long cooldown.

Mordekaiser is easily kited early. Abuse this. Always respect Mordekaiser's R when he's ahead. Gnar has very limited space to kite in death realm. Mini and Mega Gnar's Q will remain in the realm it was thrown in right before his R connects. Gnar cannot ult Mordekaiser into death realm's wall. Look to all-in based on his W charge and his R cooldown.

Nasus has no way to close the gap against you. Gnar can easily zone him out of stacking his Q because Nasus is a melee champion. Freezing the lane close to your tower is extremely efficient at preventing him from stacking. It also allows for easy ganks since he is immobile.
Nautilus is a very easy matchup because he will be building health items. Mini Gnar's W will shred through him. Gnar also has a lot of options to dodge Nautilus' hook.

Neeko relies heavily on hitting her E. Trade with her when it's on cooldown. She can also disguise herself during roams which can be devasting if you're not aware of it. Her ult's zone will be invisible if she casts it while disguised. Poke with Q and all-in after level 6.
Nocturne has fairly strong lane pressure early. Armor helps here. Once he hits level 6, he will look to all-in you if he's ahead or he'll look to roam. All-in after level 6 if his W his on cooldown.

Olaf's early levels in lane can't be beat. The key to this matchup is to dodge his axes. If he hits one axe, it's extremely easy for him to hit more because of the slow. His Q's cooldown is lowered if he picks his axes back up. Look for trades when he misses his axes. The less health he has, the more attack speed and healing he gets, so be very careful fighting him when he's low. Olaf's R allows him to not be CC'd, so all inning as Mega Gnar is not possible when he has it up.

In this lane, you absolutely have to avoid being hit by his W as it’s his primary source of damage. Once he applies Brittle on you, his next auto will do bonus damage and knock you back. Ornn will use his Q to poke, but it also opens the option of him using his E. If his E hits the terrain created by his Q, he’ll knock everything up in a circle surrounding it. Prioritize attacking him when he tries to buy items in lane because it’ll cancel it.

Pantheon is very similar to Renekton in lane. Watch his resource bar very closely and base trades off of this. His empowered Q does a lot and is also a ranged ability, so you'll see Pantheon try for this a lot into Gnar. Pantheon has to get fairly close to you in order to all in, so pay attention to your positioning. The most annoying thing about this matchup is his W. It's pretty much Braum's shield, so you can't proc your W on him if he's facing you. A good way around this is to curve Gnar's Q around him and proc it from behind since he can't turn around while using it. Pantheon's E is a gap closer, but not one you have to worry about much if you are positioning correctly. Once he hits level six, be careful with staying in lane for too long after he resets because it acts like a teleport early. Armor is your friend in this matchup, especially if he is building Lethality.

Stay away from terrain in this lane. Poppy’s E will stun if she pins you to terrain. This will lead to a devastating trade. Her Q is fairly easy to dodge. Poppy’s W will eat Gnar’s E, so be sure not to use your cooldown until the duration of her W is over. A good Poppy will be able to read when you are going to E.
Qiyana has a lot of burst early, so look to play safe. Armor is a must. Look to all-in her when she's low on mana.

Quinn's early game is pretty scary, but luckily Gnar has a pretty easy time poking her out of lane. Play this lane pretty safe early and poke with your Q. Avoid being hit by her E when you all in with your E as Mega Gnar. Her E will push you back midjump.

Renekton’s early game is extremely strong, so play very safe. Keep an eye on his Fury because his abilities gain extra effects and deal extra damage. Renekton’s E can only be cast twice if he hits something with the first cast of his E. Be very careful when approaching your minions because he will use them to get that extra cast. Gnar is able to kite Renekton very easily.

Rengar's passive makes him very mobile in top lane. This matchup can be very difficult if you don't play the waves correctly. Let his minions push to you and freeze the wave under your tower. This makes it so that Rengar can't abuse the bushes he has available to him in top lane. You can also shove the wave in, but this is rather difficult to do against Tiamat. You want to avoid bushes completely. Once Rengar hits level six, he gets a lot of roam pressure. Rengar's empowered W is a cleanse, so time your CC carefully. All inning with Mega Gnar is possible when he doesn't have his empowered W.

Riven has a lot of gap closers to get to you. Her E completely nulls out your Q damage. This lane is all about cooldowns. When Riven uses her abilities, take advantage of her. Be very careful of her R when low because her slash is an execute. Play this lane safe early and consider rushing Ninja Tabi.

Rumble’s Q is his main source of damage and Gnar outranges it. Avoid being hit by his E because it will let Rumble close the gap against Gnar to get his Q in range. His W is on a low cooldown and will always eat your Q damage. Once Rumble gets his R, be very careful. His R will slow you, deal a ton of damage, and ultimately lead to your death. Consider rushing MR in this matchup.

Ryze is a monster at clearing waves. This can make it difficult for Gnar to get lane priority. If Ryze is constantly pushing, ask your jungler for ganks. Be careful when he marks you with his E because it makes Ryze's abilities gain bonus effects. He is significantly weaker early, so look for plays then. Sadly, Ryze has the option to build Frozen Heart in this matchup. If he chooses to do this, know that you can't win trades.

The Sett matchup is very similar to the Darius matchup.
Sett wins early until Gnar gets Phage and Ninja Tabi.
After this, you have enough range and movement speed to kite Sett.
Sett will use his Q to get closer to you and then he generally wants to use his E to pull you into a charged W.
All you have to do to avoid this is use Gnar's E to escape Sett's E.
Do not go for trades unless your E is up as Mini Gnar.
If you are close enough to Mega Gnar transformation, you can go in for a trade, transform into Mega Gnar and all in.
If Sett decides to use his R here, Gnar can ult Sett into a wall immediately after Sett finishes his ult animation.
Only go for smart trades/all-ins until this power spike.

Shen’s only way to close the gap against Gnar is his E and it has a long cooldown. He can null out some of your damage with his W, but it doesn’t last for very long. Abuse him when he uses both of these cooldowns.

Singed can be a very annoying lane for Gnar, but luckily he has a lot of counter play.
Pay close attention to his mana early.
His Q uses a lot of it and it’s his only way of clearing minions.
Singed’s W will prevent Gnar from using his E.
He also has to be very close to you in order to flip you with his E.
Some Singed players will proxy the first few waves.
It’s very hard for Gnar to CS early under tower, so guard your jungler’s top side to prevent this from happening.

All of Sion’s abilities can easily be dodged. It also helps that he is a melee champion. A lot of the time, a Sion player will try to bush cheese early since his Q can be charged without giving vision, so play towards river at the beginning of lane phase. Always watch where your minions are because Sion can use his E on them to increase its range. Sion’s W will eat Gnar’s poke, but it’s on a long cooldown. When Sion is getting ganked when he has his R, he will consider using it to get away. If this is the case, flashing in front of him or using Gnar’s E to get in front of him will cause his R to collide with you, cancelling it.

Swain is very weak early and burns through mana rather quickly. Watch closely to his E usage. Punish him when he misses. If it hits, he has the opportunity to all-in you after level 6. His R takes a good bit to charge up early, but always respect the amount of healing he's able to drain from large minion waves.

Sylas' sustain makes it very difficult for Gnar to trade with him. He also has a gap closer and some range. Just Sylas being on the enemy team can hurt your team tremendously because he can steal your ult and use it whenever he wants without Gnar's Rage barrier. As you can imagine, a Gnar ultimate that isn't gated by Rage is devasting. Be very careful and be sure to let your team know when he grabs your R.

Teemo’s Q will blind, which is a nightmare for Gnar since he is an AA champion. Luckily, with Teemo’s Q being on cooldown, Gnar can abuse him. This is the key to winning lane. Stay out of Teemo’s range early to avoid being poked. Trade with Gnar’s Q. Since Teemo is squishy, you can easily push him out of lane or go for an all in with Mega Gnar. Once Gnar gets his R, all inning Teemo as Mega Gnar will almost always work out in your favor. Getting an early Oracle Lens will help you clear out his mushrooms.
Trundle is fairly easy to play against. He does have ways to close the gap against you with his pillar and his E. Avoid dueling him when he uses his R on you. Abuse him being melee.

Tryndamere can very easily be abused with Gnar because of him being a melee champion.
Avoid going in for trades against Tryndamere when he has a lot of Fury because he gets increased crit chance and his Q will also heal him a lot.
It takes Tryndamere has to AA to gain Fury, so abuse this.
His E and W will help him close the gap against Gnar.
All inning Tryndamere can be difficult when he has his R, so try and bait it out.
Prioritize Randuin's Omen as your third item to ease his crits.
If Tryndamere is split pushing, consider picking up a Phantom Dancer to help with dueling him.

Urgot’s AA range is very short compared to Gnar’s. This lane is all about dodging Urgot’s Q. If he lands his Q, his W becomes a problem because it’ll lock on to Gnar through minions. Urgot’s E is his primary way of gap closing. When Gnar is low on health, avoid Urgot as much as possible because his R is an execute.
Viktor can be a tricky matchup because of his mobility and safety from his Q. He can also clear waves very fast once he upgrades his E. Poke with your Q and look for all-ins after level 6.

The counter to poke is sustain and sadly, Vladimir can do this incredibly well. To make matters worse, he is also a ranged champion. Vladimir’s W also makes him invulnerable. This makes all inning him as Mega Gnar almost impossible because he can W your CC. In order to win this matchup, you need to avoid his empowered Q and bait out his W before an all in. Poking him to death is impossible because of the amount of sustain he has.

Wukong has a very strong early game. Because Mini Gnar has very little health early, Wukong's burst can very easily kill you in a couple of his combos. Play safe early and poke with Q. Once you get armor, look for trades/all-ins.

Yasuo is an absolute nightmare for Gnar. His E can be used indefinitely as long as he has minions to use it on. Because of this, Gnar’s only option to stay at a range is to step far from his own minion wave. The best time to trade with Yasuo is when he has no minions to E through. Watch carefully for when Yasuo has his tornado. Yasuo’s W will eat Gnar’s Q and put it on the full cooldown. It’ll also stop Mega Gnar’s Q from travelling.

Yorick’s only way to trade with you is if he lands his E. His E will slow and mark you, causing his Mist Walkers to jump to you. You absolutely have to dodge this ability. Yorick can raise his Mist Walkers if three or more graves are created. Watch very carefully for this since this is most likely when Yorick will try to trade with you. Save your E for when Yorick hits his E or casts his W. Avoid all inning him when his Maiden is attacking you because Yorick will extra damage to you.
